'''Sina Ruth Greenwood''' is a New Zealand mathematician whose interests include [[continuum theory]], [[discrete dynamical system]]s, [[inverse limit]]s, [[set-valued analysis]], and [[Volterra space]]s.{{r|directory|gauld}} She is an associate professor of mathematics and Associate Dean Pacific in the faculty of science at the [[University of Auckland]].{{r|directory}}

==Education and career==
Greenwood's parents emigrated from [[Samoa]] to [[Whanganui]] in New Zealand, shortly before Greenwood was born; they moved from there to Auckland when she was a child. She earned a bachelor's degree at the [[University of Auckland]], and after some time in Australia became a secondary school teacher in Auckland.{{r|gauld}}

Returning to the University of Auckland for graduate study in mathematics, she earned a master's degree and then completed her PhD in 1999, under the joint supervision of [[David Gauld (mathematician)|David Gauld]] and David W. Mcintyre. Her dissertation was ''Nonmetrisable Manifolds''.{{r|gauld|mg}}<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Greenwood |first=Sina |year=1999 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Nonmetrisable Manifolds |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/697 |url=https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/697}}</ref> She and three other students who finished their doctorates at the same time became the first [[topology|topologists]] to earn a doctorate at Auckland.{{r|gauld}}

After postdoctoral research, funded by a New Zealand Science and Technology Post-Doctoral Fellowship, she obtained a permanent position at the University of Auckland as a lecturer in 2004,{{r|gauld|lecturer}} later becoming an associate professor.{{r|gauld}} Beyond mathematics, her work at the university has also included advocating for the interests of [[Pasifika New Zealanders|Pasifika]] and [[Māori people|Māori]] students.{{r|gauld|lecturer}}

==Recognition==
Greenwood is a Fellow of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]],{{r|fellow}} elected in 2018.{{r|gauld}}
